title.suggested: Tom Allen, Former Champion, Dies at the Baptist Hospital

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat reported that Tom Allen, retired champion pugilist, died at the Baptist Hospital on April 5, 1903, and that a recent will left nearly everything to his nurse, Mrs. Hartgrave.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Globe-Democrat, Monday Morning, April 6, 1903, page 1. Full headline: 'Champion Tom Allen Has Gone to His Rest.'

facts.fact: Allen died at the Baptist Hospital, Garrison and Franklin avenues, at 7:35 a.m. on April 5, 1903, after being very low for several days
places: Baptist Hospital, Garrison and Franklin avenues, St. Louis

facts.fact: Allen was taken to the Baptist Hospital on Friday, March 27, 1903, after three months of poor health
Allen was born in Birmingham, England, on April 23, 1839
According to his own record Allen fought fourteen prize-ring matches in England and ten in America
Allen's last fight, by his own record, was with Jim Stewart in England on March 10, 1879, for £50 a side; it lasted fifty-five minutes and sixteen rounds and Allen won

Allen opened a saloon near the present Boatmen's Bank, Fourth Street and Washington Avenue, in 1868 (last digit faint, could be 1863) and remained a tenant of the real estate firm J. C. Kaime & Bro. ever since
places: Fourth Street and Washington Avenue, St. Louis

facts.fact: At the time of his death Allen kept 'Tom Allen's Champion's Rest' at 619 Market Street
places: Champion's Rest, 619 Market Street, St. Louis

facts.fact: A will made a few weeks earlier, witnessed by Dr. Heine Marks and Dr. C. A. Newcomb, left $10 to each of his daughters, Mrs. 'Polly' Taylor of St. Louis and one in England, and the rest to Mrs. Hartgrave, his housekeeper and nurse
The paper said Allen had left a wife in England

A man at the opening of Allen's strong box in a safe deposit vault said it held only $500; claims by the Hyde Park brewery ($350) and others, paid by Mrs. Hartgrave under power of attorney, used up all but a small balance

notes: Recrop needed: include the full two-column headline and the second column of the obituary (below the portrait, ending '…after 64 years of eventful life on two continents'), and drop the Shiloh story above it. The 1868/1863 saloon date should be checked against the image (1868 fits his 1867 arrival). The will's '$10 to each daughter' differs from the index's '$10 to each of his two sisters'.
